evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game does not impose a rule or constraint that is incompatible with any other story in the backlog.
Inviting estimators via a URL is compatible with other stories; no conflicting permission or behavior found.
Starting a round by entering an item does not conflict with any other story's constraints or behaviors.
Seeing all items to be estimated is compatible with other stories and imposes no incompatible rule.
Selecting an item to be estimated or re-estimated is consistent with other stories.
Adding items during a session does not create incompatibilities with other backlog stories.
Editing an item in the list is compatible with other stories and does not impose conflicting constraints.
Deleting an item from the list is not inconsistent with any other requirement in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: This allows revealing estimates before all estimators have given theirs, which conflicts with PP-033 (require simultaneous reveal after all have given) and with participant stories that require ability to change until the final reveal (e.g., PP-034, PP-041).
Accepting the average of estimates as moderator action does not conflict with other constraints in the backlog.
Auto-filling the estimate when unanimity occurs is compatible with other stories and not inherently conflicting.
Entering the agreed-upon estimate is consistent with other stories and imposes no incompatible behaviors.
Re-estimating a previously estimated story is compatible with other backlog items.
Importing stories from a spreadsheet does not impose rules that conflict with other stories.
Copy/paste from a spreadsheet is a compatible behavior and not contradictory to other stories.
Browsing previous games is not inconsistent with any other story's requirements.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript (stories and estimates) can be implemented without violating other stories (e.g., data could be anonymized for research), so no clear incompatibility in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting transcripts as HTML can be implemented in ways that do not conflict with other stories (e.g., respecting privacy/storage rules), so no direct conflict identified.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV export for further processing does not inherently conflict with other backlog items; privacy/export format can be addressed without contradiction.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Providing deletion of a game is not incompatible with other stories; it coexists with view/export functionality as long as ordering/permissions are handled, so no direct contradiction in backlog.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation requirements do not conflict with other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login functionality is compatible with other stories; no incompatible constraints found.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Updating account details does not conflict with other requirements.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion that removes stored data is not inherently incompatible with other stories (deletion can coexist with viewing/exporting when sequencing/permissions are defined).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying local timezone is not contradictory with other backlog items.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder by email does not impose behavior or rules that conflict with other stories.

evaluations.rationale: Providing choice of card sets does not conflict with other requirements.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting invites to 15 is not incompatible with other stories in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name
evaluations.rationale: Estimator joining by name does not conflict with other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item under estimation is consistent with other stories.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Browsing the list of items is compatible with other requirements.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Showing that an estimator has given an estimate (presence indicator) can coexist with requirements to reveal estimates simultaneously and does not by itself create an incompatible rule.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This requires simultaneous reveal only after all have given their estimate, which conflicts with PP-009 that allows the moderator to show estimates immediately before all have played.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: This grants the ability to change until the final reveal; it conflicts with PP-009 which permits revealing estimates before all estimators have played, thereby preventing that ability.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates per estimator is compatible with other stories; it does not inherently contradict storage or reveal rules in backlog.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying who gave which estimates (typically after reveal) can be implemented without conflict with other stories; no explicit incompatible rule found.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Shared timer functionality does not conflict with other requirements in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting the timer when all have played is not incompatible with other stories; it defines a behavior that coexists with reveal rules.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Historic browsing of stories and estimates is compatible with other backlog items; no conflicting constraints identified.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card order consistency does not impose rules that conflict with other stories.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allows changing until draw completion; conflicts with PP-009 which permits the moderator to show estimates immediately before draw completion, preventing this ability.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying thumbnails during play is a UI preference and does not, by itself, conflict with other stories (privacy/storage can be handled separately).

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance does not conflict with any other backlog requirements.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is compatible with all other stories and not contradictory.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database performance optimizations do not impose incompatible behaviors or constraints relative to other stories.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance does not conflict with other requirements in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance expectations are compatible with other stories; no incompatible constraint found.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support does not conflict with other backlog items.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design requirement is not incompatible with other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong

evaluations.rationale: Storing research results non-identifiably can coexist with UI features that show identities in-session or with transcripts if implementation separates research datasets; no direct incompatible rule in backlog forces identification in stored research data.
